argument_summary: The present record does not support clean policy compliance, but it does support a narrower certification posture: limited initial launch with explicit acknowledgment that support is weak and rests on operational containment rather than full closure of the Spanish-language refund-guidance gap. Aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, a 7% initial rollout, and rollback/monitoring are relevant evidence that the launch is operationally controllable. The overbroad claim is that those controls alone satisfy policy. A more accurate position is that certification can be defended only on a caveated basis if the auditor distinguishes operational readiness from policy-complete readiness and avoids treating the current record as full compliance.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim is made that business cost changes the policy standard. The practical reason to avoid escalation is narrower: the existing evidence shows some operational containment and reversibility, so remaining uncertainty can be handled as a bounded caveat rather than treated as requiring a stronger adverse conclusion than the record supports.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against any claim of clean compliance on the current record. The admissible evidence shows the affected multilingual customer support use case remains exposed, and the available risk acceptance is only a draft with no approver and no explicit coverage of that exposure. Under the stated policy, rollout controls, monitoring, and rollback do not by themselves remove the disclosure or approved-risk-acceptance predicate. The defensible reinterpretation is therefore not that policy is satisfied in full, but that the record supports only a caveated certification posture with explicit recognition that policy support is incomplete.
concessions: The current record does not support a finding of clean compliance.
The multilingual customer support segment remains in scope despite the unresolved Spanish-language refund-guidance gap.
The risk acceptance document is incomplete and does not explicitly cover the exposed segment.
Limited rollout, rollback, and monitoring are relevant mitigations but are not substitutes for the policy-required disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
